$comment: Brief: price the date family's interaction layer on Base UI by building ONE
component honestly, then extrapolate. Everything below is measured on this
tree unless a field's name says 'estimate'. Estimates are labelled and their
basis is stated; nothing is recalled.

what_was_built.public_api: frozen — DateFieldProps, DateBounds, BoundKey, DateFieldSize and the three variant exports are byte-identical to the baseline
what_was_built.arithmetic_source: @internationalized/date (standalone, zero React dependency — unchanged by the migration)

the_premise_confirmed.method: ls of the installed dist's subpath directories
the_premise_confirmed.arithmetic_evidence: PersianCalendar.getDaysInMonth(Esfand 1404) = 29, getDaysInMonth(Esfand 1403) = 30, getMaximumDaysInMonth() = 31, getMonthsInYear = 12 — all answered identically with no React library present

line_count.$comment: total = every line. code = comments and blank lines stripped. Lumo's documentation standard is a real cost, so both are given.

supporting_edits.packages/core/src/strings.ts: +39 lines (4 new announced strings per locale — the words react-aria's patched fa-IR bundle used to supply)
supporting_edits.packages/ui/src/provider.tsx: +17/-1 (mount the Lumo locale context alongside I18nProvider)
supporting_edits.scripts/build-registry.mjs: +2 SHARED_COMPANIONS entries so the copy-in closure still compiles

line_count.$multiplier_note: 349 / 39 and 950 / 248. The code multiplier is the honest one: the baseline's 39 code lines were a wrapper, and the 349 are an implementation.

hours_equivalent.measured_scope: one agent session, 22:48–23:08, including 4 render probes, 2 mutation checks and the new test file
hours_equivalent.human_equivalent_basis: estimate, not a measurement. Grounded on: the artifact is 349 code lines plus 601 lines of the documentation Lumo requires, and the four probes that produced the Field/SSR and CalendarDate-constrain findings were the expensive part — each is a render-and-read cycle a human would also have to run.
hours_equivalent.parity_basis: estimate. The gap list under not_done is 16 behavioural props plus paste/IME/AT behaviour that jsdom cannot test, so parity requires real-device screen-reader work this environment cannot do at all.
hours_equivalent.honest_summary: At THIS fidelity, one date component is about a day. At PARITY with what React Aria already ships, it is closer to a week for the calendar-based members. The two numbers are different answers to different questions and the library needs the second one.

survived: ArrowUp on the DAY segment commits Esfand 30 in 1403 and commits NOTHING in 1404
the MONTH segment cycles 12 -> 1 within the year, keeping the day
the MONTH segment decrements 1 -> 12, landing in Esfand
a filled date field renders its segments in Persian digits
an EMPTY date field shows the locale's own segment names, not English
DateField renders zero English announced strings
DateField renders a description and points aria-describedby at it
the empty-segment value is «خالی» and appears once per editable segment
an unbounded Lumo field renders no FieldError element at all
the_unedited_suite.$note: The other 30 assertions cover Calendar, RangeCalendar, TimeField, DatePicker, DateRangePicker and the react-aria patch bundles. Those five components were NOT migrated, so those assertions are still grading React Aria and prove nothing about Base UI.

assertions_that_pass_for_the_wrong_reaso.$comment: The most important section. A green suite was not accepted at face value; it was mutation-tested.

locale_provenance.finding: 6 of the 8 DateField assertions pass because Lumo's own locale context DEFAULTS to fa-IR, not because the <I18nProvider locale=fa-IR> the test mounts was read. Base UI has no locale context and cannot see React Aria's.
locale_provenance.measurement: flipping LumoLocaleContext's default from fa-IR to en-US turns exactly those 6 red; the I18nProvider in the test is unchanged and has no effect either way
failing_under_en_US_default: ArrowUp on the DAY segment commits Esfand 30 in 1403 and commits NOTHING in 1404
a filled date field renders its segments in Persian digits
an EMPTY date field shows the locale's own segment names, not English
DateField renders zero English announced strings
DateField renders a description and points aria-describedby at it
the empty-segment value is «خالی» and appears once per editable segment
locale_provenance.consequence: the assertion survives; the mechanism behind it does not. Every remaining date component inherits this, and so would any future locale.

the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.finding: dates.test.tsx's headline entry assertion — the one the roadmap treats as proof that Jalali is verified for ENTRY — cannot distinguish a correct implementation from one that silently commits the wrong date.
the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.root_cause: new CalendarDate(persian, 1404, 12, 30) does not throw and does not hold 30. The constructor CONSTRAINS and returns 1404-12-29. Measured. Likewise 1403-12-31 -> 1403-12-30.
the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.measurement: deleting the explicit calendar.getDaysInMonth guard from date-field-state.ts's toValue leaves all 39 assertions in dates.test.tsx GREEN. The test's case asserts only that no non-null value arrives, and the constrained date equals the previous value, so no onChange fires at all.
the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.the_defect_that_hides_there: a field displaying ۱۴۰۴/۱۲/۳۰ whose committed value is Esfand 29 — the user's date, off by one, with nothing visible to see
the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.closed_by: packages/ui/src/date-field-entry.test.tsx, 'two ArrowUps from Esfand 28 of a COMMON year commit 29 and then nothing', which starts a day earlier so the two behaviours produce different onChange sequences
the_leap_rule_assertion_is_weaker_than_i.verified: that new test goes red under the same mutation while dates.test.tsx stays green

first_byte_defect.finding: Base UI's Field applies aria-labelledby and aria-describedby in a LAYOUT EFFECT, so neither exists in the served bytes.
first_byte_defect.measurement_server:
label

description

— no aria-labelledby, no aria-describedby
first_byte_defect.significance: this is the same failure shape the audit pinned on React Aria's useSlotId(), found in Base UI, on the axis Base UI was predicted to win
first_byte_defect.consequence: dates.test.tsx asserts the description association on SSR output, so Field.Control cannot carry this component's ARIA. Ids are minted with useId and wired by hand in render.
first_byte_defect.cost: the association logic is ~8 lines here and would repeat in all six components

base_ui_field_primitive.dangling_label_for: Field.Label emits for=<control id> even with no Field.Control present, pointing at an id nothing carries. Worked around with nativeLabel={false} and a span render.
base_ui_field_primitive.field_error_unusable: Field.Error matches against a native control's ValidityState; this component has no native control.

not_done.$comment: Enumerated by asking the compiler for Exclude<keyof DateFieldProps, handled | DOM | ARIA>. The public API type is UNCHANGED, so tsc is silent about every one of these.
not_done.$dom_note: the React Aria build ended in {...props} so every unnamed prop still reached AriaDateField; this build destructures seven and drops the rest, including id, style, onFocus, onBlur, onKeyDown and aria-describedby

capabilities_absent.validation: no engine at all. minValue/maxValue/isDateUnavailable are typed by DateBounds and enforced nowhere; cycling is not clamped and the field never marks itself invalid. This is a MISSING FEATURE, not a fix — it is also why the English/Gregorian FieldError defect cannot appear: there is nothing to produce a message.
capabilities_absent.form_integration: the field submits nothing and <Form> cannot see it. No hidden input.
capabilities_absent.time_segments: hour/minute/second/dayPeriod are not built, so TimeField cannot be derived from this engine as it stands and CalendarDateTime loses its time half silently
capabilities_absent.era_segment: not emitted. Persian has one era so it does not bite here; Japanese and ROC calendars would get a wrong field.
capabilities_absent.paste_ime_selection_drag: React Aria handles a paste into a segment and an IME composition. This handles keydown only.
capabilities_absent.assistive_tech_workarounds: React Aria carries a documented pile of TalkBack/VoiceOver spinbutton workarounds. None reproduced, and none testable in jsdom — this is the category that does not show up in a green suite and does show up for users.
capabilities_absent.live_announcements: no live region; React Aria announces segment changes and calendar navigation

could_not_test_here: real screen-reader announcement of role=spinbutton under NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver/TalkBack
IME and paste behaviour (jsdom has neither)
next build / full pnpm run verify — out of scope by the brief's RAM rule; the Integrate agent owns the one verify

coupling_the_family_cannot_be_migrated_o.finding: date-picker.tsx, date-range-picker.tsx and time-field.tsx all import renderSegment, DateBounds and DateFieldSize from date-field.tsx. renderSegment renders a React Aria <DateSegment>.
coupling_the_family_cannot_be_migrated_o.consequence: renderSegment was left on React Aria so those three keep compiling and dates.test.tsx could be run unedited. The library therefore now contains TWO segment implementations. A DatePicker contains a date input, so migrating the field without the picker is not a shippable state.
coupling_the_family_cannot_be_migrated_o.real_unit_of_migration: the family of six, not the component

copy_in_closure_growth.note: two new shared modules enter the dependency closure of every date component a consumer copies

extrapolation_to_all_six.$method: grounded on the size of what React Aria actually supplies, counted in its own shipped dist (non-minified .mjs, intl string tables excluded because those are locale data, not interaction). This turns the extrapolation into a ratio rather than a guess.

measured_point.$covered_note: shared_segment_engine + date_field_own, at PARTIAL fidelity — see not_done
measured_point.$ratio_note: 0.157 Lumo code lines per upstream dist line. It is high compression because the skipped features are exactly the verbose ones: validation, form integration, granularity branching and AT workarounds.

projection_at_this_fidelity.why_it_understates: the calendar's roving-focus day grid does not compress the way segment code does. Its complexity is focus management across month boundaries, live-region announcements and per-cell state (today / outside-month / selected / unavailable / range-start / range-end), and none of that has the 'skip the branch' escape the field's granularity handling had. Treat the calendar members as at least 1.5x this projection.

per_component_estimate_days_to_this_fide.$basis: estimate, scaled from the measured date-field session by the upstream line ratios above

per_component_estimate_days_to_react_ari.$basis: estimate. Adds validation, form integration, granularity, prop passthrough, paste/IME, live-region announcements and real-device screen-reader verification — the last of which cannot be done in this environment at all.

the_number_that_matters.question: is this a week of work per component?
the_number_that_matters.answer: no at this fidelity, yes at parity for the calendar-based members
the_number_that_matters.detail: One date component reached a demonstrable, test-backed state in one session and about 350 code lines. Six of them, at the same fidelity, is roughly two working weeks. Six of them at parity with what React Aria already ships is roughly four, and the last stretch is screen-reader work on real devices that no gate in this repo can grade.
the_number_that_matters.why_not: the cost is bounded and the arithmetic — the part that is genuinely hard and genuinely Persian — ports untouched. @internationalized/date is standalone and stays. What is being rebuilt is keyboard plumbing, which is tedious rather than risky.
what_should_change_the_plan_instead: the date family must be migrated as a family, in one change, not one component at a time — measured, see coupling
the locale context must land BEFORE any further Base UI component that announces or formats anything, or each one silently invents its own locale resolution
dates.test.tsx must gain the Esfand-28 case before the migration, not after — it is currently unable to fail on a class of silent off-by-one, and that is true on React Aria today as well
budget the calendar separately from the other five; it is the single largest piece and it is the one this round did not touch

tests_run: packages/ui: coverage.test.ts, provider.test.tsx, patch.test.tsx, hydrated.test.tsx all pass
repo_state.verify_not_run: per the brief's RAM rule; the Integrate agent owns the one verify
repo_state.registry_note: registry.json was ALREADY stale on this branch before this round — the 13 earlier rebuilds never regenerated it, so gate:registry would have failed regardless. Regenerating it here produced 102 insertions, most of them the earlier rebuilds' @base-ui/react dependency entries.
repo_state.$concurrency_note: those three appeared in the working tree during this session and carry tsc errors of their own. They belong to another agent and were not touched.
